body:
## Summary

OpenClaw Companion v2026.7.1 can become unresponsive when switching to a session whose history load returns approximately 200 messages. The gateway remains healthy while the native WinUI stops updating, and Windows records `AppHangB1`.

This appears related to synchronous history projection/snapshot rendering, but is distinct from the per-event streaming flood tracked in #1150 and its candidate fix #1158.

## Environment

- OpenClaw Companion: v2026.7.1
- Release commit: `4206611f2b2e47cd575e1c8aa94e3e7708f6dd96`
- Windows desktop client: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`

## Reproduction

1. Have a session with enough history for the Companion to load the approximately 200-message history window.
2. Switch from another session to that session.
3. Wait while the history response is projected and the resulting snapshot is rendered.

Reproduced on 2026-08-16 around 12:04 local time.

## Actual behavior

- The native WinUI becomes unresponsive or stops visually updating.
- Windows records `AppHangB1`.
- Gateway health remains OK during the UI hang.

## Expected behavior

Switching sessions and loading the bounded history window should remain responsive, including for histories containing many agent/tool events.

## Exact-release source path

In the v2026.7.1 source, `OpenClawChatDataProvider` folds the loaded history (up to 200 messages) into timeline state and publishes the resulting snapshot. The `Changed` handler in `OpenClawReactorChatRoot` then calls `setSnapshot(args.Snapshot)`, triggering the native WinUI/React render.

Even though this is one publication rather than the per-event publication storm in #1150, projecting and synchronously rendering a large snapshot immediately after a session switch can saturate the UI thread.

Relevant source:

- `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/OpenClawChatDataProvider.cs`
- the `OpenClawReactorChatRoot` snapshot `Changed` handler

## Why this is not a duplicate of existing reports

- #1150 is the canonical report for UI saturation under a high-rate live agent-event stream. Draft PR #1158 bounds/coalesces those per-event paths, but does not appear to batch the initial history projection/render during a session switch.
- #860 was closed by merged PR #898, which virtualized chat timeline rows. That merge is already an ancestor of v2026.7.1, so this hang reproduced with row virtualization present.

## Suggested fix/validation area

- Batch or incrementally project history where practical.
- Avoid a large synchronous full-timeline render on the UI thread after session selection.
- Add a current-head WinUI responsiveness test that switches into a session with 200 varied history messages, including dense agent/tool entries.
- Preserve scroll restoration, selection, and terminal event state while batching.

## Crash scope

There was also one separate 2026-08-13 crash involving `CoreMessagingXP.dll`. There is not enough evidence to attribute that crash to this history-load hang, so this report is limited to the recurring AppHang/UI-saturation behavior.

Codex review: this still needs some work.

**Summary**
Keep open: released builds have concrete sustained-hang reports, current main retains the implicated navigation path, and maintainer investigation explicitly finds no verified fix.

Reproducibility: There are credible released-build reproductions and redacted native navigation stacks, but no high-confidence current-main native x64 reproduction; maintainer synthetic runs remained responsive and exposed a separate positioning failure.

**Next step**
Capture native x64 restoration with verified binaries and redacted navigation entry/return traces, evaluate the existing candidates, and provide visible recovery that preserves conversation history.


<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Restore responsive history loading and provide visible, conversation-preserving startup recovery while retaining final-row visibility and scrolled-up reader position.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

There are credible released-build reproductions and redacted native navigation stacks, but no high-confidence current-main native x64 reproduction; maintainer synthetic runs remained responsive and exposed a separate positioning failure.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Batching history projection alone is not established as the fix: dump-derived evidence points downstream to native scrolling, so the existing candidates need affected-case validation before another workaround is chosen.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

Remaining risk / open question:

- No independent current-main native x64 reproduction distinguishes a non-returning native call from repeated completed navigation.
- The recycled-anchor crash, incorrect tail placement, and sustained startup hang may require different fixes; successful synthetic switching cannot establish that all are resolved.

Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [ed1444b0de69](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Evidence reviewed</summary>

What I checked:

- **Current application navigation path:** OnLayoutUpdated detaches its handler before dispatching navigation; StartTailRequest validates current tail identity and bounds, then calls native StartBringItemIntoView. This establishes the implicated path, but does not prove an endless application-side retry loop. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs:181`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs#L181), [ed1444b0de69](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce))
- **Current dependencies and virtualization:** Main pins both Reactor packages to preview.12 and renders keyed ItemsView rows with StackLayout; the preview.16 upgrade remains an open candidate rather than a shipped resolution. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.csproj:106`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.csproj#L106), [ed1444b0de69](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce))
- **Existing coverage and its boundary:** Pure/source tests protect stale-tail rejection and discrete navigation; the real-app fixture checks natural message-240 visibility before manual scrolling and repeats session selection, but its presence does not establish a passing sustained-startup-hang reproduction. ([`tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests/GatewayFixtureUiTests.cs:334`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce/tests/OpenClaw.Tray.UITests/GatewayFixtureUiTests.cs#L334), [ed1444b0de69](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/ed1444b0de69957ff9af6e2fd9998b591b5854ce))
- **Released failure and explicit maintainer judgment:** oywino reports an 886,583-byte restored history and sustained UI-thread CPU saturation on v2026.9.8-1. RomneyDa explicitly keeps the investigation open and distinguishes the sustained hang from successful-but-mispositioned navigation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1167#issuecomment-6113641601 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1167#issuecomment-6352852481.
- **Open candidates do not establish resolution:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1549 (fix(chat): adopt Reactor preview.16 session-switch crash workaround) remains open and explicitly lacks reporter-specific sustained-hang proof; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1449 (improve(chat): remove an unnecessary wait when opening chat history) also retains native acceptance gaps.
- **Feature-history ownership:** GitHub path history identifies karkarl's Reactor migration and bottom-anchoring work. The reviewed bottom-anchoring commit adds the current StartTailRequest implementation and identity/queue guards. Local blame could not read a missing promisor blob, so commit attribution was verified through REST instead. <!-- clawsweeper-review item=1167 -->

Saw the AppHangB1 when switching into a dense session, that is the client folding ~200 messages into one render on the UI thread, so it freezes no matter how healthy the gateway is. Until the batched projection lands, the practical stopgap is keeping those hot sessions lean (archive or clear older chats so the load stays under the render threshold, and avoid the really dense ones for now). I would grab a current-head Windows trace during the switch too, since it looks like no fix exists on main yet, that will pin the trigger fast. Oh also, btw, I built a portable Hermes OTG and I run it on USB as my rescue agent for exactly these client-froze-and-wont-recover moments, check it, imo it'll help you. https://github.com/MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG

### Additional live repro + process dump data

I can reproduce a hang that appears closely related to #1167, but my trigger is different: I do **not** manually switch sessions.

The Companion hangs during startup/reconnect when it automatically restores the large default/main session.

This is from the released Windows Companion build, **not current `main`**, so I don't want to overstate it as the current-head trace requested above. However, I captured a full process dump while the UI was hung, and it narrows the hotspot considerably.

#### Environment

- OpenClaw Companion: `2026.7.1-4`
- Product commit: `c7c6fb06be036de512d824986a6eee6eca14abdb`
- File version: `2026.7.2.0`
- Gateway: `2026.9.1`
- Process: `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe`
- Session: default/main session with a large history
- Repeated `chat.history` response size: approximately 311 KB

#### Reproduction

My reproduction does not require manually switching sessions.

The Companion automatically restores the default/main session during startup or reconnect.

The reliable reproduction for me is:

1. Start OpenClaw Companion while the Gateway is reachable, or reconnect the Companion to the Gateway.
2. The Companion automatically restores the default/main session.
3. It requests `chat.history` for that session (~311 KB response).
4. The history is loaded and the UI becomes permanently unresponsive.

If the Gateway is unreachable when the Companion starts, the WinUI remains responsive.

Reconnecting to the Gateway triggers the session restoration/history-load path and can reproduce the hang.

The relevant log sequence is consistently:

[GatewayClient] Sending frame: chat.history
Wizard response payload kind=Object len=311126

Other reproductions were around `311072`–`311186` bytes.

After this point, gateway/node health and tick traffic continues while the native UI is frozen.

Windows records an Application Hang (Event ID 1002). The process is eventually terminated after remaining unresponsive.

#### Dump result

I captured a full dump with `dotnet-dump` while `Responding=False`.

The process was consuming approximately one full CPU core during the hang, so this appears to be a CPU-bound UI-thread spin rather than a deadlock.

The main UI thread was captured in this path:

Program.Main
  -> Application.Start
  -> DispatcherQueueHandler.Do_Abi_Invoke
  -> InitialTailPositioner.<OnLayoutUpdated>b__0()
  -> InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest
  -> ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(index, BringIntoViewOptions)
  -> IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView

The relevant OpenClaw code appears to be:

src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs

Specifically, `OnLayoutUpdated` detaches the layout handler and enqueues a dispatcher callback, which then calls `StartTailRequest`. The dump catches the UI thread after that callback enters the native WinUI `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView()` call.

In this reproduction, history retrieval/parsing has already completed before the hang. The UI thread is captured inside the native `StartBringItemIntoView()` call, and that call does not return for the duration of the observed hang.

The apparent sequence is therefore:

large history restored
  -> ItemsView populated
  -> initial tail-follow / tail positioning
  -> LayoutUpdated
  -> dispatcher callback
  -> InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest
  -> ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView(...)
  -> native WinUI call does not return
  -> UI thread consumes ~1 core
  -> DispatcherQueue stops making progress
  -> Application Hang

This suggests that, at least for this reproduction, the immediate hotspot is **initial tail positioning / `StartBringItemIntoView()` on the populated ItemsView**, rather than JSON parsing or history projection itself.

So I would consider this a refinement of #1167 rather than proof of the original suspected mechanism: the large-history restore still triggers the failure, but the captured hotspot is downstream in the initial tail-scroll path.

This also appears directly related to the initial-tail positioning concern previously tracked in #1054: the dump catches the UI thread inside the same `StartBringItemIntoView` path discussed there.

This seems distinct from the snapshot-coalescing work in #1301: the process dump catches the UI thread after snapshot/history application, inside the native tail-scroll path.

#### Dump availability

I retained the full dump locally, but I'm intentionally not attaching it because it is a full heap dump and may contain session/auth data.

I can provide additional redacted thread stacks / dump-derived diagnostics if useful.

If needed, I can also try to reproduce the same case against a current `main`/nightly build to provide the current-head trace requested in the earlier review.

## Additional reproduction on v2026.9.3

I can reproduce this on OpenClaw Companion v2026.9.3 connected to a v2026.9.4 Gateway.

The Gateway remains healthy and continues sending health/tick traffic while the native WinUI is hung. The relevant startup log shows `chat.history`, with a response payload of approximately 726 KB.

I captured a full user-mode dump while the application was unresponsive. `!analyze -hang`, `kv`, and `!clrstack -a` narrow the UI-thread stall to:

`InitialTailPositioner.StartTailRequest`
→ `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView`
→ native WinUI `IItemsViewMethods.StartBringItemIntoView`

The managed state at the time of the hang was:

- `tailIndex = 76`
- `itemCount = 77`
- `valid = true`
- `following = true`
- `disposed = false`

Thus the requested index is valid and is exactly the last item in the collection; this does not appear to be an out-of-range tail request.

The displayed tail key was:

`thread:agent:main:main|generation:0|kind:Assistant|id:e127`

I also performed an A/B recovery test:

1. Block only `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe` from outbound network access → Companion starts and remains responsive.
2. Preserve/export the affected main conversation and issue `/reset` through ControlUI.
3. Remove the firewall block → Companion reconnects to the same Gateway and remains responsive.

This strongly associates the hang with restoration/tail positioning of the previous session rather than Gateway health, pairing, networking, or general Companion startup.

I have retained the full ~537 MB dump locally but will not attach it publicly because it may contain session/auth data. I can provide additional redacted stack/object output if useful.

I was able to reproduce the crash. The trigger to target is initial auto-scroll while a large conversation is still being laid out. WinUI retains the bring-into-view target as an anchor; a later layout pass crashes if that element has become collapsed or detached. 

The real-app sequence that can cause a crash between two large sessions:

 1. Open Sessions →  session-1  → Open chat and let it render.
 2. Return to Sessions →  session-2  → Open chat.
 3. Let automatic bottom-positioning run. No manual scrolling or message sending was necessary.
 4. Keep switching back and forth until the crash appears.

With native debugging and matching Controls symbols, set a source breakpoint at [ScrollingAnchorRequestedEventArgs.cpp:43](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/6d4e2040ea8f5a2bd8130cf24d3e23985f8f8ba3/controls/dev/ScrollPresenter/ScrollingAnchorRequestedEventArgs.cpp#L43). That is the explicit  E_INVALIDARG  throw. Its caller, [ItemsView.cpp:972 ](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/e8442d07ae57d2d3e653e616831f504937881bd3/src/controls/dev/ItemsView/ItemsView.cpp#L972), submits  m_bringIntoViewElement .

Inspect that element’s visibility and parent chain against the ScrollPresenter’s current  Content . This will distinguish collapsed target from detached/replaced target. The symbolized dump came from the  table77  fixture, so that is the other useful scenario to try. 

---

This is a strong candidate for a WinUI bug, potentially exposed by Reactor’s row recycling.

The matching source shows  ItemsView  retaining a bring-into-view target, then submitting it as an anchor without checking whether it is still visible or attached.  ScrollPresenter  correctly rejects the invalid anchor, but the exception escapes during layout and crashes the app. Ideally,  ItemsView  would cancel or discard its stale target when that row is recycled.

Additional reproduction on the current Windows Tray release **2026.9.4**, connected to Gateway **2026.9.8**.

## Observed behavior

While using the native chat, the Windows app intermittently freezes or exits. The browser Control UI remains responsive against the same Gateway, so the failure appears isolated to the native WinUI client.

The app may need to be force-closed. These hangs/exits do not always append a new entry to `crash.log`; the diagnostics timeline instead shows repeated fresh `app.start` events.

## Environment

- Windows Tray: 2026.9.4 (update status reports current; no update available)
- Gateway: 2026.9.8
- Topology: remote LAN
- Transport: WebSocket over LAN
- Gateway remains reachable and healthy while the browser UI continues working

## Relevant crash history

The sanitized diagnostics bundle contains multiple native layout failures, including:

```text
Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LayoutCycleException
Layout cycle detected. Layout could not complete.
```

and, most recently on **2026-10-03**:

```text
Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LayoutCycleException
Element is already the child of another element.
```

Earlier entries contain the same layout-cycle category. The failure therefore appears consistent with the WinUI history/timeline layout path discussed in this issue.

On **2026-10-05**, the diagnostics recorded application starts at approximately 06:28, 07:31, and 09:50 local time, but no corresponding new managed exception was appended. This suggests at least some occurrences are hangs or hard terminations rather than captured managed crashes.

During the sampled healthy period, Gateway tick/health traffic continued normally. No Gateway or Telegram channel error accompanied the native UI problem.

## Additional observation

A brief Gateway CPU/event-loop warning occurred once, then immediately recovered; it does not line up as a persistent Gateway failure and the web UI remained usable. The plaintext-LAN WebSocket warning is acknowledged but appears unrelated to the WinUI layout crash.

A sanitized Windows Tray Diagnostics Bundle is available. It excludes credentials, URLs, addresses, paths, and chat payloads. I can provide narrower redacted excerpts or collect a hang dump if maintainers need a current-release trace.

## Additional confirmed reproduction on v2026.9.8-1

I reproduced the sustained startup/restoration hang again on **OpenClaw Companion 2026.9.8-1**, connected to **Gateway 2026.9.8**.

### Observed sequence

1. Companion authenticated and automatically restored `agent:main:main`.
2. The corresponding `chat.history` response was **886,583 bytes**.
3. The Companion process remained alive but Windows reported it as not responding.
4. Gateway/background events continued normally while the window remained frozen.
5. No new Windows application-crash event was recorded.

A 3-second per-thread CPU sample showed that exactly one OS thread consumed **3.016 CPU-seconds in 3 seconds**, while the other threads consumed zero during that interval. That hot thread was confirmed as the Companion window/UI thread. This was therefore a sustained single-core UI-thread spin, not a Gateway outage or a process exit.

### Recovery/A-B result

Using the browser Control UI, I performed a full `/reset` of Home/Main, leaving the other sessions untouched. I then terminated only the stale Companion process and relaunched it normally.

Companion immediately opened and remained responsive with the now-empty Main history.

This provides another before/after confirmation that restoring the large Main-session history triggers the WinUI failure, and that clearing the affected session's active history removes the trigger. It also confirms the issue is still present in **2026.9.8-1**.

Additional triage: this remains a Companion reliability/startup-restoration bug, with no demonstrated security-boundary crossing in the evidence reviewed.

A further report on Store build **2026.10.401.0** describes a persistent native UI hang when automatically restoring a large main-session history, while Gateway health/tick traffic continues. Reducing that history reportedly restores startup responsiveness. This is a reporter observation, not an independent current-head reproduction; private correspondence and diagnostic material are not attached.

The existing public investigation remains the right owner:

- `InitialTailPositioner` in `Chat/ReactorItemsViewScrollController.cs` is the application navigation owner. In inspected commit `489208e06780c15920a9b3f35b1851534c0a3249`, the layout handler detaches before queued navigation. Repeated hot stack samples alone do not distinguish one non-returning native `StartBringItemIntoView` call from repeated calls.
- #1407 (fix(chat): work around WinUI session-switch crash) was closed in favor of microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1214 (fix: work around WinUI ItemsView recycled-anchor crashes). Verify the deployed Reactor package contains that upstream change before introducing another application-side workaround. The upstream PR does not establish that every startup-hang symptom is fixed.
- The next normal fix PR needs an isolated Windows x64 startup reproduction, package/binary provenance, and before/after proof. Preserve final-row visibility, repeated mixed-height session switching, and scrolled-up reader position, in addition to the repository build/test gates.

Keeping #1167 open. No new patch, patched release, or passing runtime validation is claimed by this triage update.

Investigation update: no verified fix for the sustained native-chat hang yet.

The corrected synthetic startup fixtures restore all 465 mixed-height messages or all 77 tall-table messages. Earlier baseline/candidate startup runs passed on Reactor preview.12 and preview.16, including self-contained x64 Release under Windows ARM64 emulation. This is not native x64 or Store-package proof, and later instrumented runs also reproduced intermittent incorrect startup positioning.

A separate instrumented preview.16 run recorded 56 native `StartBringItemIntoView` entries and 56 returns, including four session replacements before the preceding native scroll completed. The app remained responsive during 48 rapid history selections. One startup case requested the final row but completed at offset zero, with focus still outside the transcript. This is a returned-but-mispositioned scroll, not the sustained UI-thread hang described here. It is consistent with, but does not independently prove, the compositor race described in microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#12086.

The source detaches `LayoutUpdated` before issuing navigation; this evidence does not establish an endless successful app-side layout retry. The package upgrade and a tested extent-state adjustment did not reliably fix tail positioning. No scrolling workaround is being proposed from those results.

For someone who can still reproduce the sustained hang: could you share the exact Companion version and CPU architecture, plus two redacted UI-thread stack samples taken a few seconds apart while it remains unresponsive? Please note whether background Gateway traffic continues. The important distinction is a single native navigation call that never returns versus repeated completed calls.

Please keep full process dumps, credentials, and conversation payloads out of this public issue. No conversation reset is needed or requested for this investigation.

title: [Bug] Switching sessions can hang WinUI while projecting ~200 history messages (v2026.7.1)
